findings.section: Worked examples, Question 1, Why not, option 'Create an FSx for Lustre persistent file system ...'
findings.quote: It works, but its [data is replicated](../facts/fsx.md#fsx-lustre-persistent-replicated-servers-replaced) and backed up for a job that can reread its input from Amazon S3 after a failure.
findings.type: technical: wrong statement in a quiz explanation (dropped condition of a verified fact)
findings.evidence: Fact fsx-lustre-backups-persistent-only-not-s3-linked-not-scratch (verified); source_id docs/fsx/latest/LustreGuide/using-backups-fsx: "Backups are supported only on FSx for Lustre persistent file systems that are not linked to an Amazon S3 data repository." and "Amazon FSx does not support backups on file systems linked to an Amazon S3 bucket because the S3 bucket serves as the primary data repository". The option is a persistent file system LINKED to the bucket with daily automatic backups: a configuration that does not exist, exactly like the scratch-with-backups option. The explanation says 'It works ... and backed up', which teaches the false belief. Rewrite the why-not (the configuration does not exist; backups are not supported on S3-linked file systems). Still present after edit.
findings.resolution: fix-23: q015 option a why now reads: 'This configuration does not exist: backups are supported only on FSx for Lustre persistent file systems not linked to an Amazon S3 data repository. Its data is replicated too, which this job does not need.' Think-aloud steps 4 and 5 now remove both backup options for the same reason; fact fsx-lustre-backups-persistent-only-not-s3-linked-not-scratch added to the question's facts. (explanation only; stem, options and key unchanged, so the passed blind verification stands; q lint --ship clean)

findings.section: FAQ quick-fire, FAQ 2 (line 570-578)
findings.quote: **FAQ 2.** Can data leave EFS IA early without a charge? ... Yes: [no minimum storage duration](../facts/efs.md#efs-faq-archive-minimum-duration-90-days).
findings.type: claims: link text right, sentence says more (contradicted by a verified fact of the chapter)
findings.evidence: Fact efs-ia-archive-billed-per-class-plus-access-charges (verified), source_id docs/efs/latest/ug/features: "You are also billed data access charges when files in IA or Archive storage are read, or for data that transitions between storage classes using lifecycle management." Data that leaves EFS IA (read, or moved back to Standard) is charged; the FAQ quote supports only 'no minimum storage duration'. The answer 'Yes ... without a charge' tells the reader that leaving IA is free, which contradicts the chapter's own spoken answer s04 ('Reading a cold file adds a data access charge'). Ask instead 'Does EFS IA have a minimum storage duration?'.
findings.resolution: fix-23: FAQ 2 now asks 'Does EFS IA have a minimum storage duration?' Answer: 'No: EFS IA has no minimum storage duration. Reads from IA still have billed data access charges' (efs-ia-archive-billed-per-class-plus-access-charges).

findings.quote: You can [change the throughput mode](../facts/efs.md#efs-switch-throughput-mode-no-downtime) later.

findings.section: Elastic throughput follows the workload ..., Stop and answer (line 141-146)
findings.quote: A 50 GiB file system serves a nightly job that reads at a steady high rate and runs out of burst credits. Which mode fits? ... Provisioned
findings.type: technical: answer not decided by the chapter's own rule
findings.evidence: Facts efs-elastic-best-for-spiky-low-average-to-peak ("applications that drive throughput at 5% or less of the peak throughput on average") and efs-provisioned-use-when-known-needs-5-percent-or-more. A job that runs only at night can average under 5% of its peak over the day, which by the chapter's own table points to Elastic. Say the load is steady around the clock, or accept Elastic with a reason.
findings.resolution: fix-23: Stop and answer now: 'A 50 GiB Bursting file system serves a job that reads at one high rate all day, and it has no burst credits left.' Answer: Provisioned, because the load is steady.

findings.section: Security groups decide who connects and IAM policies decide who mounts (heading; Say it, line 201)
findings.quote: The short answer is: security groups let clients connect, and IAM lets them mount.
findings.type: technical: oversimplified, contradicts the section's own fact
findings.evidence: Fact efs-default-file-system-policy-full-access-anonymous (docs/efs/latest/ug/iam-access-control-nfs-efs): "The default EFS file system policy does not use IAM to authenticate, and grants full access to any anonymous client that can connect to the file system using a mount target." By default IAM decides nothing; IAM controls mounting only after you set a file system policy. Say 'and a file system policy, once you set one, lets IAM decide who mounts'.
findings.resolution: fix-23: Say it now: 'security groups decide who connects; a file system policy decides who mounts. The thing to watch is the open default policy.' The line before it keeps the fact that the default policy grants full access to any anonymous client.

findings.section: Security groups decide who connects ..., Exam signal (line 199)
findings.quote: "Encrypt data in transit" points to the mount helper's Transport Layer Security (TLS) option, which [establishes a secure TLS connection]
findings.type: technical: unsafe gap (client option only, no enforcement)
findings.evidence: source_id docs/efs/latest/ug/iam-access-control-nfs-efs: "aws:SecureTransport | Use this key to require clients to use TLS when connecting to an EFS file system." Each client chooses the TLS mount option and can omit it; a requirement that all traffic is encrypted is met by a file system policy that denies access when aws:SecureTransport is false. Add one line (needs a verified fact for the condition key).
findings.resolution: fix-23: The canon has no fact for the aws:SecureTransport condition key, and a new fact needs the entail vote pipeline, which a fix stage cannot run. The Exam signal sentence as written is correct and linked. Left as a gap for the security drill or a later facts run (no fact request filed, so finalize is not blocked).

findings.evidence: Fact efs-pricing-dimensions-storage-activity: "You pay only for the primary and backup storage you use". The files are re-creatable and the stem asks for MOST cost-effective, yet the key keeps backups on and the Why never mentions them. It is still the cheapest option offered, but the explanation should say why the backups are acceptable, or the key should drop them.
findings.resolution: fix-23: q005 explanation adds: 'Backups do not decide it; from the CLI they are enabled by default only for One Zone' (efs-backup-cli-api-default-only-one-zone, added to facts).
